newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Camdessus, IMF mission to visit Moscow soon.
newsitem.headline: Camdessus, IMF mission to visit Moscow soon.

text.p: International Monetary Fund director Michel Camdessus will visit Moscow soon following talks between Russian officials and the fund's team monitoring Russia's economic performance, an IMF official said on Monday.
Interfax news agency said the visit would take place from April 1 to April 3, but no agenda had yet been agreed.
Former economy minister Yevgeny Yasin said earlier on Monday that the regular monitoring mission would arrive in Moscow on Wednesday to finalise talks on Russia's 1997 economic programme.

"The most difficult problems concern the budget, its expenses and taxes," Yasin told a news conference. He said First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais had authorised him to continue talks with the IMF.
"These problems will be discussed on Wednesday when the (IMF) mission arrives in Moscow."

The IMF is checking Russia's performance each month before deciding whether to release tranches of a $10 billion three-year loan. It has already postponed several tranches amid doubts about Russia's ability to collect taxes and meet budget plans.
The 1997 economic plan, a key factor behind payments this year, will outline plans for structural reforms and set targets for the year.

Russian officials say the IMF is particularly insistent on reforming natural monopolies such as national power utility Unified Energy System (UES), the Railway Ministry and Gazprom natural gas producer monopoly.
New First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov has lashed out at the monopolies for their high prices, which he said was hindering economic growth.
